Stacy came on to finish the race. Brown's car made it around to the pits
under its own power.

HOT PURSUIT
Fred Lorenzen, Elmhurst, Ill. (#28-
1958 Ford) was giving it all he had as
he roars into the south turn ahead of
Roger Ward, Indianapolis (#99-1958
Ford) in the Sept. 20, 1959 250 mile late
modél stock car race at state fair park.
Lorenzen took the lead on the i28th
mile and held it to the end. Ward vainly
sought to catch the blonde youngster
but never did quite make it and finished
second. Lorenzen later went on to win
his second consecutive national United
States Auto Club late model stock car
title.
MONEY SMILE
It was a happy Tony Bettenhausen,
Tinley Park, Ill. the checker flag greeted
in the July 19, 1959 150 mile late model
stock car race here. Tony was filling in
for Roger Ward who had a previous com-
mitment and it was a worthy substitu-
tion. Tearing Tony grabbed the lead at
the end of the first mile and never re-
SMOKI
linquished it. Victory to him was worth
nearly $4,000. It was Bettenhausen's
third major stock car race win here in
six years.
(Army Krueger Photo)
SPEEDWAY SCRAMBLE
Roy Czach, Chicago (#40-1957 Ponti-
ac) spun in the north turn on the 71st
mile in the Aug. 23, 1959 150 miler held
during fair week and that started a chain
reaction of trouble. Bill Cheesbourg,
Tucson, Ariz. (#18-1958 Ford) spun to
avoid Czach's car but still'hit him.
Duane "Red" Duvall, Hammond, Ind.
(#87-1958 Ford) also caromed'into
Czach's car. All three cars were out of
the race and Czach spent the night at a
Milwaukee hospital under observation
when he complained of chest pains.
(Ralpb Eicholz Photo)
